claim: On one WSL2 workstation, the same fixed Codex 0.159.3 task that must call one MCP tool was run three times against llama-server (llama.cpp release v0.5.0, build b11146) and three times against Ollama v0.35.0, both serving the same Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M GGUF on the CPU. Under the frozen pass rule neither arm passed the gate: llama-server passed 0 of 3 scored runs and Ollama passed 2 of 3, so the predicted result (llama-server fails, Ollama passes) did not occur as preregistered; the MCP tool call itself completed in 0 of 3 llama-server runs and in 3 of 3 Ollama runs, and the one Ollama run that failed (B3) had its tool call completed and then hit the wrapper's 300-second wall limit before the final answer.

pass_rule: A run passes when its codex exec --json event log has a completed mcp_tool_call item for server time, tool get_current_time, with a result carrying a datetime string, and the last agent_message contains that string. An arm passes when all three scored runs pass.

deviations_from_preregistration: The comment line of codex-config/config.toml.tmpl was corrected and the scratch config re-rendered nine seconds after the preregistration hash was taken and before the first model call; only a comment changed.
No scored run was repeated, excluded or re-scored; the prompt, the pass rule, the pins, the model and the serving settings were not changed after the preregistration.

The scorer's reason for arm A's runs can read tool_call_failed: the model called Codex's own function tools read_mcp_resource and list_mcp_resources, which Codex reports as mcp_tool_call items. The preregistered reason list did not foresee that; the field target_tool_called was added to the receipt to say whether get_current_time itself was ever called. The pass rule is unchanged.
run_notes: B3: the first model call took 4m35s (prompt at 49.56 and generation at 3.30 tokens per second, against 93.38 and 8.20 in warm-up B on the same server and prompt), the MCP tool call then completed at 23:46:43Z, and the 300-second wall limit ended the run 24 seconds into the second model call, before a final answer. The gate ran one server at a time; the workstation is shared and what else loaded the CPU during B3 was not measured.
A1: the model, not having been given get_current_time, tried Codex's read_mcp_resource four times with guessed URIs until the 300-second wall limit.
A2 and A3: the model answered that get_current_time is not available (A3 after a failed list_mcp_resources call).
deviations_from_brief: CPU instead of GPU on both arms, decided before the first run: llama-server could not allocate more than about 4.5 GiB on the GPU although nvidia-smi reported about 16 GiB free (cudaMalloc out of memory in three attempts).

ollama launch codex was used only to write the Codex profile and model catalog (with -- --version); the scored runs call codex exec --profile ollama-launch directly, as upstream's profile-based setup documents.
Arm A uses the model catalog that Ollama's launcher wrote, so that Codex sends the same instructions and tool list to both servers.
The Codex config keys were read from the source at the tag, not from the hosted config reference.
limitations: One workstation, CPU inference, one model (Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M), one prompt, three scored runs per arm; this is a local integration check, not a test on the new machine.
Only the function gate was measured: no speed, quality or GPU comparison.
Context was 32768 tokens on both arms; Ollama's Codex page asks for at least 64k, which this model cannot provide.
llama.cpp was tested at its latest release (v0.5.0, build b11146); later prerelease builds were not run and PR #23235 is still open.

llama-server's verbose log shows the converted request, not the raw one; that Codex sent two namespace tools rests on the server's own warning lines and on Ollama counting twelve tools where llama-server kept ten.
Ollama 0.35.0 itself runs the GGUF through a bundled llama-server (its log says so); the difference measured is in the Responses layer in front of it.
llama.cpp documents no Codex setup at this pin; arm A's Codex profile mirrors the one Ollama's launcher writes.
Sampling temperature was 0.6, so runs are not deterministic.

Two scored runs ended at the wrapper's 300-second wall limit (A1 and B3). On CPU each model call takes one to several minutes, so the limit, not the server, decided B3's verdict; the gate was not re-run with a longer limit.
manifests/stack.json has no Ollama component, so component_ids name llama-cpp and codex only; the receipt is not registered in manifests/evidence.json.
OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 and loopback binding were set; outbound traffic was not captured.
